title: Theory of the Status Quo: From Unmet Childhood Needs to the Metacrisis

nodes.title: Felt safety
nodes.text: The child's experience of being safe, created by a caregiver who protects it. Brown counts it among five conditions for secure attachment, and it supports every area of development. (Brown)

links.label: Brown & Elliott: The Five Primary Conditions that Promote Secure Attachment (handout)

nodes.title: Attunement
nodes.text: Feeling seen and known: a caregiver who responds accurately to the child's behaviour, to its inner states and to what it is ready for at its stage. It supports self-esteem and the child's growing understanding of its own mind. (Brown)

links.label: Brown & Elliott: The Five Primary Conditions that Promote Secure Attachment (handout)

nodes.title: Comfort & Soothing
nodes.text: Felt comfort: a caregiver who soothes and reassures the child when it is distressed. Repeated over time, this supports the child's ability to regulate its own emotions. (Brown)

links.label: Brown & Elliott: The Five Primary Conditions that Promote Secure Attachment (handout)

nodes.title: Support to explore
nodes.text: Felt support for the child's best self: a caregiver who encourages it to explore, both outwardly in the world and inwardly in its own interests and abilities. It supports the development of the child's own self. (Brown)

connections.assumptions: No visible linking symbol for this row (unlike the rows above) — pairing inferred from position only.

links.label: Brown & Elliott: The Five Primary Conditions that Promote Secure Attachment (handout)

nodes.title: Expressed delight
nodes.text: Feeling valued: a caregiver who visibly delights in the child. It supports the child's self-esteem and its awareness of its own mind. (Brown)

connections.assumptions: No visible linking symbol for this row — pairing inferred from position only.

links.label: Brown & Elliott: The Five Primary Conditions that Promote Secure Attachment (handout)

nodes.title: Connection
nodes.text: Survival style built around the need for contact. Where early connection was frightening or absent, a person may protect themselves by withdrawing from contact and from their own body and feelings. (Heller, NARM)

nodes.title: Thinking
nodes.text: Retreating into analysis and abstraction to keep feeling at a distance, so that the person stays rational and emotionally detached.

nodes.title: Spiritualizing
nodes.text: Using spiritual ideas or practice as an escape, so that painful feelings are avoided rather than felt.

nodes.title: Attunement
nodes.text: Survival style built around the need to have one's own needs recognised and met. Where caregivers did not sense them, a person may learn to stop noticing, or asking for, what they need. (Heller, NARM)

links.label: NARM Training Institute: What is NARM?

nodes.title: Trust
nodes.text: Survival style built around the need to rely on others. Where care proved unreliable or manipulative, a person may come to depend on control and self-sufficiency instead. (Heller, NARM)

connections.evidence: Arrow from Trust box to "craving for power / 'nobody can be trusted'".
Arrow from Trust box to "compulsive soothing" strategy.

links.label: NARM Training Institute: What is NARM?

nodes.title: Autonomy
nodes.text: Survival style built around the need to become one's own person. Where independence met pressure or guilt, a person may struggle to set limits and to say what they want. (Heller, NARM)

connections.evidence: Arrow from Autonomy box to "greed, craving for more".
Arrow from Autonomy box to "fear of dependence, urge towards separation".

links.label: NARM Training Institute: What is NARM?

nodes.title: Love-Sexuality
nodes.text: Survival style built around the need to be loved and to bring heart and body together. Where love felt conditional, a person may feel unlovable or keep affection and sexuality apart. (Heller, NARM)

connections.evidence: Arrow from Love-Sexuality box to "perform (to be loved, worthy): career, status, money".
Arrow from Love-Sexuality box to "hunting sexual attraction".

links.label: NARM Training Institute: What is NARM?

nodes.title: Craving for numbing
nodes.text: Addiction to substances, entertainment, ADHD. Tuning out what one feels: addiction is read as an attempt to relieve pain, and ADHD as a tuning-out rooted in early stress rather than simple pleasure-seeking. (Maté)

connections.assumptions: Several strategy boxes converge on this area of the drivers column; exact 1:1 source→target pairing not fully resolvable from the photo.
connections.evidence: Arrow drawn from this strategy cluster into the metacrisis-drivers column, landing near "erosion of collective sensemaking".
Short arrows from numbing into the first drivers (open question 5).

nodes.title: Craving for control, safety, immunity
nodes.text: Seeking safety through dominance: if I rule, nobody can hurt me. Collectively it can appear as claims of superiority over others.

connections.evidence: Short arrow from control/supremacy into the first drivers.

nodes.title: Scape goating, projection the blame
nodes.text: Placing a feeling too large to bear, often shame, onto another person or group and blaming them for it. Done collectively it can license hostility and violence.

nodes.title: Craving to be seen?
nodes.text: A hunger for attention and recognition, which may trace back to not having been sufficiently seen as a child.

nodes.title: Craving for power: "nobody can be trusted"
nodes.text: Having concluded that nobody can be trusted, a person seeks power over people and situations so as not to depend on them.

nodes.title: Compulsive soothing
nodes.text: Food, work, shopping or similar habits used to calm the nervous system. Maté reads such habits as short-term relief from pain rather than a cure for it, which is why they tend to repeat. (Maté)

connections.evidence: Crossing arrows from compulsive soothing on the board.
Crossing arrows from compulsive soothing on the board.

nodes.title: Greed, craving for "more"
nodes.text: A craving for more that can stay hungry however much arrives, because what is being sought is not what is being acquired.

nodes.title: Fear of dependence, urge towards "separation"
nodes.text: Needing others feels dangerous, so closeness is avoided and distance is treated as safety.

nodes.title: Perform (to be loved, worthy)
nodes.text: Pursuing career, status or money to earn love and worth, as if being loved depended on achievement.

connections.evidence: One of two arrows leaving Perform on the board.
Second arrow leaving Perform on the board.

nodes.title: Narcissism
nodes.text: A grand self-image that defends against feeling unworthy and depends on continued admiration. Maté describes it as arrested development from unmet early needs rather than a fixed trait. (Maté)

nodes.title: Hunting sexual attraction
nodes.text: Pursuing sexual attention, possibly as a substitute for love and recognition that went unmet.

nodes.title: Erosion of collective sensemaking
nodes.text: The weakening of a society's shared ability to agree on what is true and what matters, so that it cannot respond well to its problems. Schmachtenberger ties it to an information environment that rewards outrage and certainty over understanding. (Schmachtenberger)

connections.evidence: Arrow toward "collective 'freeze'" in the structures column.

links.label: The Consilience Project: Democracy and the Epistemic Commons

nodes.title: Collective disempowerment
nodes.text: Many people feel unable to change anything and stop trying (German: "Ohnmacht", powerlessness).

nodes.title: Lacking willingness to radical change / regulate
nodes.text: Even where the problems are understood, the will to change course radically or to accept binding rules is missing.

nodes.title: Racism + (post)colonialism
nodes.text: Racism, together with the structures and stories of domination that colonial rule left behind and that persist after it formally ended.

nodes.title: Multipolar traps
nodes.text: "If I don't do it, someone else will; I can't compete." Each actor does what is locally rational and the combined result is bad for all; escaping it takes agreement, transparency and enforcement together. (Schmachtenberger)

nodes.title: Race to the bottom
nodes.text: "If we tax or regulate, companies move to the Bahamas." Competition between places or firms pushes standards down.

nodes.title: Race to market
nodes.text: Privatise the upside, externalise the risk: in a first-mover race, whoever ships first captures the gain while others bear the costs. Schmachtenberger counts market races among the main forms of multipolar trap. (Schmachtenberger)

links.label: The Consilience Project: Development in Progress

nodes.title: Arms race
nodes.text: For example nuclear weapons, AI and bioweapons: each side builds up because the other might. (Schmachtenberger)

nodes.title: Consumerism cluster
nodes.text: Four mutually reinforcing features of modern economic life: consumerism, individualism, neoliberal capitalism and extractivism.

connections.evidence: Arrow drawn past the structure cards to Climate breakdown.
Arrow drawn past the structure cards to Pollution.
Arrow drawn past the structure cards to Resource & hydrocarbon depletion.

nodes.title: Consumerism
nodes.text: Buying as the usual route to satisfaction. Markets sell "pseudosatisfiers" that deepen the hunger they promise to fill. (Schmachtenberger)

nodes.title: Individualism
nodes.text: Treating the person as a self-contained unit, which can loosen ties to community and shared responsibility.

nodes.title: Neoliberal capitalism
nodes.text: An economic order centred on markets, competition and growth.

nodes.title: Extractivism
nodes.text: Taking resources and value out of nature and communities faster than they can renew.

nodes.title: Hyper agents / AI
nodes.text: "Extremely motivated and capable to accrue power." The few actors at the top of a power law who maximise their returns on agency at scale and shape the incentives and values of everyone else. Whether advanced AI becomes another such agent is a live concern. (Schmachtenberger)

links.label: Civilization Emerging: Bend Not Break, Maximum Power & Hyper Agents (Schmachtenberger)

nodes.title: Patriarchy / sexism
nodes.text: A social order in which men hold most power and authority.

connections.assumptions: Low-medium confidence — this may instead route through an unlabelled structural node.
connections.evidence: Drawn closer to the polycrisis column than the structures column; arrow appears to run fairly directly to "sexual assault", skipping the structures column.

nodes.title: Intergenerational war trauma
nodes.text: Trauma from war that can be passed on to children and grandchildren through parents' emotional availability, bodily tension and family culture.

nodes.title: Collective 'freeze'
nodes.text: A group that is overwhelmed shuts down and fails to act, like the freeze response in an individual. This is an analogy used for modelling, not an established finding.

connections.evidence: Arrow toward "dysfunctional democracy" within the same column.

nodes.title: Populism, narrative warfare
nodes.text: Politics driven by simple us-versus-them stories and deliberate manipulation of what people believe.

connections.evidence: Arrow toward "great power war / violence / genocide".
Arrow points up from populism to dysfunctional democracy on the board.

nodes.title: Lack of wisdom
nodes.text: Power that has outgrown the wisdom to use it. Schmachtenberger argues that wisdom involves restraint, and that restraint keeps losing to rivals who do not practise it. (Schmachtenberger)

links.label: The Consilience Project: Development in Progress

nodes.title: Debt + interest financial system
nodes.text: Money created as interest-bearing debt, so the system needs continual growth to be repaid. Debt papers over a widening gap between monetary claims and the energy and materials needed to honour them. (Hagens)

connections.evidence: Vertical arrow directly below, within the same column.

nodes.title: Embedded growth obligation
nodes.text: An economy that must keep growing to stay stable, whether or not growth serves people or the planet: humanity as a growth-compelled, energy-hungry "superorganism". (Hagens)

connections.evidence: Arrow fanning out into the polycrisis column.
Arrow fanning out into the polycrisis column.
Arrow fanning out into the polycrisis column.

nodes.title: Loss of community
nodes.text: Fewer lasting ties between people, with less mutual care and fewer shared places.

nodes.title: Loss of spirituality
nodes.text: The loss of shared practices that gave people meaning, awe and belonging. Vervaeke describes it as the loss of an "ecology of practices" that religion once supplied. (Vervaeke)

nodes.title: Marketing
nodes.text: Deliberately triggering and shaping desire in order to raise consumption.

nodes.title: Power politics
nodes.text: Politics conducted as a contest of strength between states and elites.

nodes.title: Great power war / violence / genocide
nodes.text: Direct war between major powers, with the violence and genocide that accompany it.

nodes.title: Extinction risk from tech
nodes.text: Technologies, such as engineered pathogens or advanced AI, that could end humanity's future.

nodes.title: Climate breakdown
nodes.text: A destabilised climate driven by greenhouse-gas emissions.

nodes.title: Meaning crisis
nodes.text: A widespread loss of purpose, belonging and orientation. Vervaeke argues that it has deep cultural and historical roots and underlies other crises. (Vervaeke)

links.label: John Vervaeke: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis

nodes.title: Pollution
nodes.text: Waste and toxins released into air, water and soil.

nodes.title: Resource & hydrocarbon depletion
nodes.text: Running down finite stocks, such as fossil fuels, that the economy depends on.

nodes.title: Ecocide
nodes.text: Destruction of ecosystems on a large scale.

nodes.title: Sexual assault
nodes.text: Sexual violence: any sexual act, or attempt of one, committed against a person without their consent.

nodes.title: Dysfunctional democracy
nodes.text: Democratic institutions that no longer turn what citizens want into workable decisions.

nodes.title: Side note: Maté's health-crisis path
nodes.text: Maté argues that the same unmet needs also contribute to individual illness, including chronic and autoimmune disease. (Maté)

schemaExtensions: Added optional per-node field `provenance`: "verbatim" (label read directly off the drawing) or "interpreted" (Jonas's own uncertainty, e.g. a question mark he drew).

Added optional per-connection field `provenance`: "verbatim" (arrow unambiguous and directly between these two boxes), "verbatim-structure" (a same-row pairing symbol, not a causal arrow), or "interpreted" (arrow direction/endpoints inferred with some uncertainty from a photographed whiteboard).

Added optional per-connection field `isFeedbackLoop: true` to mark a drawn bidirectional (two-headed) arrow. It is stored once, on one node, and means the arrow has a head at each end; a one-way arrow that merely points back to an earlier column carries no flag. 2026-10-29: the consumerism cluster <-> marketing arrow, previously stored as two flagged connections (one on each node), was collapsed into the single connection on the consumerism cluster (45 -> 44 connections); the twin's evidence text was appended as a further block. A theoryofchangebuilder.com-compatible export expands it back into the mutual pair.
No change to the existing `connections[].targetId` mechanism — it already allows any node to point at any other node, which is what makes feedback loops representable without a schema change.

Reserved (currently empty) top-level field `interventionLinks: []` for the later feature: an intervention theory of change will add entries here of the shape {interventionTocId, targetsNodeIds: [...], note}, linking back to specific node ids in this status-quo map without modifying this file's own nodes.

These are additive, optional fields — a file with none of them (e.g. a plain theoryofchangebuilder.com export) remains fully valid, and a file using them should still open correctly in theoryofchangebuilder.com with the extra fields simply ignored.
